acceptanceStatement: tools/verify_design.py v4 closes the lock shape: v4 requires exactly inventorySuccessors, contractSuccessors and inventoryPassageInheritance and refuses the singular v2/v3 slots. Both chains must be nonempty ordered lists. The first inventory hop must be parented on a selected base input and every later hop on its immediate predecessor pin, so branches, reorders and cycles refuse. Each hop keeps the full binding2 additive-inventory proof: record/review/assent joins, zero policy change, strict sorted row superset. No inventory candidate or contract member (record or candidate) may reuse any path in the accepted source/application overlay, an earlier inventory candidate or an earlier contract member. This closes CB-A01. Base inputs, all inventory candidates and all earlier contract members and records remain accepted parents; forward and cyclic contract parents refuse. The same parent and selector with a different meaning refuses across units, while identical meanings are accepted once. Every override whose parent is a non-final inventory in the chain must use a /files/N/description JSON Pointer; any other selector (line, /standing, /files/N/role, /packages/...) raises a controlled DesignError. Such overrides are projected by stable file path to the recomputed index in the final inventory, with the before and after text carried through. The lock must list exactly those projections in canonical order. A direct identical final override makes the projection unnecessary, and a conflicting direct or ancestor meaning refuses. Descriptions in the inventory bytes remain historical. v1, v2 and v3 locks still verify, including the accepted live v3 lock. The real v4 lock verifies, with passed=true, 46 inputs, inventory3 selected (4 added files), the metadata-v2 contract with 9 candidates and 4 overrides, empty inheritance and productQualification=false. The tool never writes to the architecture.

advisories.topic: the added tests do not isolate several headline v4 guards
advisories.detail: Mutation run (mutate.py, mutation-results.json; 24 mutants over successor_chain) against the 38 frozen tests. These mutants survive all 38 tests but are killed by the independent probes: M02 (inventory candidate reuse guard removed); M03 (inventory reuse limited to the chain, dropping the accepted-overlay check); M07 (unsupported inherited selector guard removed, which turns controlled refusal into an uncaught IndexError or silently wrong projection); M09 (inherited-vs-direct conflict removed, so the direct override silently wins); M10 (inherited-vs-inherited conflict removed, so the last writer wins, which UNIT.md explicitly disclaims); M11 (canonical inheritance sort removed); M15 (a direct identical final override still emits an inheritance entry). The real lock is the only thing that kills M15; no unit test does. test_inventory_branch_and_repeated_candidate_refuse exercises only a branch, not a repeated candidate. Current behavior is correct in every case (probes C06, C09, C09b, C11-C13b, C15/C15b, C17, C18, C04/C05; real-mirror R04, R10, R12). Before any lock actually uses a second inventory hop or a non-empty inventoryPassageInheritance, add isolated tests for these guards, plus a real two-hop reindex case.

advisories.topic: 'differing meanings for the same physical passage refuse' holds only per exact selector spelling (CB-A03 now spans units)
advisories.detail: Conflict detection is keyed on (parent path, selector JSON). Two separately reviewed units can override the same JSON passage through a line selector and a JSON Pointer with different meanings, and the lock still verifies. The synthetic final-inventory case is probe C25. On the real accepted inventory3 bootstrap.rs description, probe R13 uses a later unit's line selector with a conflicting after and the lock verifies. On a non-final ancestor inventory, the line alias is refused by the description-only profile (C12). This requires two reviewed and root-assented records, so it is not a present defect. Either narrow the UNIT.md wording to 'the same selector', or require JSON Pointer selectors for JSON parents in a future record profile.

advisories.topic: canonical inheritance order is lexicographic selector JSON, undocumented
advisories.detail: expected_inheritance sorts on (final path, json.dumps(selector)), so /files/10/description precedes /files/2/description (C15 passes; the numeric order in C15b refuses as 'inheritance differs'). This fails closed but will surprise lock authors. Document the order or sort numerically in a later revision.

advisories.topic: uncontrolled exception types on malformed chain entries
advisories.detail: A candidate pin with an unhashable path (e.g. a list) raises TypeError at the reuse check before inventory_successor can emit a DesignError (C27). main() catches TypeError, so the CLI still exits 1 without passing. Separately, final_rows[...] and the IndexError path in the selector projection rely on earlier guards (additive profile, M07 guard); IndexError is not in main()'s caught tuple. This is similar in kind to CB-A06.

advisories.topic: defense-in-depth code that cannot be distinguished by tests
advisories.detail: 'inherited inventory passage row changed' (M08) is unreachable, because inventory_successor already requires every inherited row to be equal by value at every hop. The seen set (M22) is always a subset of accepted. Both are harmless equivalent mutants, and no test can kill them.

CB-A01 is resolved: reuse now refuses against the whole accepted overlay for contract members (C19, R09; killed by the tests via M05) and for inventory candidates (C18; not covered by the tests, see B4-A01). CB-A02 (splitlines line numbering), CB-A04 (record shape not closed), CB-A05 (float/int equality in joins; now also applies to the immediate-predecessor dict comparison) and CB-A06 still apply, because selected_passage, contract_successor and same_reference are byte-identical to accepted binding3. CB-A03 is superseded by B4-A02. CB-A07's older survivors are unchanged.

It approves no future inventory or contract unit. Every multi-hop and inheritance behavior was exercised only with synthetic reviews and assents: in temp fixtures, or on a temp mirror of real bytes. No real second hop or non-empty inheritance exists.

The base source45/application46 approval, the substance of inventory3 and metadata-v2, and the semantic correctness of their passage overrides were not reaudited. They rely on their existing accepted reviews and root assent.
The arch working tree has unrelated uncommitted modifications. Verification relies on exact pins, not git state. The product repository has no commits.

Probes cover the successor_chain guards and v1-v3 compatibility at the level of passing/refusing locks. The older v1-v3 guards were not re-mutated (see CB-A07).
